headline: Semilab lifts revenue, but integration costs hit profit
summary_short: Onto Innovation's Q1 2026 revenue rose 9.5% y/y to $291.9M, boosted by the newly acquired Semilab USA business, but net income fell 47.3% y/y to $33.8M ($0.67 diluted EPS) as acquisition-related amortization, inventory step-up costs, and restructuring charges compressed margins.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.5% y/y to $291.9M, with Semilab USA contributing $27.1M and higher advanced-packaging and logic/memory sales offsetting a decline in advanced-node customers. Gross margin fell to 50.1% from 53.7% y/y on $6.1M of Semilab step-up amortization and higher restructuring-related inventory write-downs, though margin rose 3.7ppt sequentially as those one-time costs eased. Operating expenses rose to $112.9M on $19.7M of acquisition-driven intangible amortization (vs $8.4M) and Semilab integration/ERP costs, pushing operating income down 46.9% y/y to $33.5M. Net income fell 47.3% to $33.8M ($0.67 diluted EPS). Cash and securities combined rose to $654.2M. On April 20, 2026 the company agreed to acquire 27% of Rigaku for ~$710M, partly funded by a $500M bridge loan. No numeric guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by the Semilab USA acquisition ($27.1M revenue contribution) plus higher sales to advanced-packaging and logic/memory customers, partly offset by lower advanced-node customer sales.
Growth reflects $27.1M of incremental Semilab revenue outweighing $6.1M of inventory step-up amortization and higher restructuring-related inventory write-downs.

Y/y compression reflects higher restructuring-related inventory write-downs and $6.1M of Semilab step-up amortization; margin still rose 3.7ppt sequentially as those costs eased from the prior quarter.

Decline reflects a $19.7M intangible-amortization charge (vs $8.4M) from the Semilab acquisition, $5.2M of restructuring and severance costs (vs $1.1M), and higher G&A from Semilab integration and ERP costs.
Compression is arithmetic: operating income fell 46.9% while revenue grew 9.5%, driven by the acquisition-related cost increases described above.
Decline tracks the drop in operating income, plus lower net interest income after using cash to fund the Semilab acquisition in Q4 2025, partly offset by lower foreign-currency losses.
Margin fell arithmetically as net income declined 47.3% while revenue rose 9.5%.
Decline tracks the net-income drop; weighted basic shares were roughly flat y/y (49.2M to 49.7M), so dilution is not a material factor.
Decline tracks the net-income drop; weighted diluted shares rose only 1.2% y/y (49.4M to 50.0M) from Semilab-related share issuance, adding modest incremental dilution.
Cash used for $179.5M of marketable-securities purchases and $6.7M of stock-award tax payments outweighed $26.3M of operating cash flow; combined cash and marketable securities still rose to $654.2M.
Growth reflects $33.8M of retained net income in the quarter, partly offset by $6.7M of stock-award tax withholding and other comprehensive losses.

Management highlighted 9.4% sequential revenue growth from Semilab and advanced-packaging demand, and disclosed an April 20, 2026 agreement to acquire 27% of Rigaku for ~$710M, funded partly by a $500M Goldman Sachs bridge loan, expected to close in H2 2026.
